short: Broke with Rome to remarry, and made the crown head of the English church.
full:
Henry VIII spent his first twenty years as a conventional Renaissance prince, campaigning in France and leaving administration to Thomas Wolsey. Everything turned on the succession. When the papacy would not annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, Thomas Cromwell steered through Parliament the statutes that severed the English church from Rome: the Act in Restraint of Appeals in 1533 and the Act of Supremacy in 1534, which made the king Supreme Head of the Church of England.

The dissolution of the monasteries between 1536 and 1541 transferred perhaps a quarter of the land in England to the crown, and then to the gentry who bought it, which made the break irreversible. It also provoked the Pilgrimage of Grace, suppressed with executions. Henry married six times, executed two wives and two chief ministers, and left three children who each ruled in turn. He died at Whitehall in January 1547, obese, ulcerated and in debt from renewed war with France.
